Alcohol-associated hepatitis: 3

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient improves after hospitalization for alcohol-associated hepatitis. Which long-term treatment priority addresses a major driver of recurrent injury rather than focusing only on whether the aminotransferases normalize at discharge?

  1. Supportive but not diagnostic AST predominance
  2. Assess and treat malnutrition
  3. Evaluate infection and treatment contraindications
  4. Support sustained alcohol abstinence
  5. Alcohol-associated hepatitis
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Support sustained alcohol abstinence

Treatment includes care for alcohol use disorder rather than focusing only on short-term liver tests.

Understanding the options

Support sustained alcohol abstinence
Treatment includes care for alcohol use disorder rather than focusing only on short-term liver tests.
Alcohol-associated hepatitis
Recent jaundice after sustained heavy alcohol exposure can suggest alcohol-associated hepatitis, but competing causes must be assessed. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Supportive but not diagnostic AST predominance
AST greater than ALT can support the context but cannot diagnose alcohol-associated hepatitis by itself. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Assess and treat malnutrition
Nutritional deficits are common and need active assessment and support. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Evaluate infection and treatment contraindications
Severe disease treatment decisions, including corticosteroids in selected patients, require assessment of infection and other risks. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
